answer: Each identity files one ferrous shaving from a claimed vein, in a velvet pouch keyed to its serial, and locks a 70-credit bond. A raven auditor assays every shaving and groups filings by shared fingerprint: shavings from one rented farm share one vein print, so the whole group is exposed and all its bonds burn, while a lone filing passes. First filing costs 36 credits; the k-th fake costs 36+6(k-1), each fake needing a fresh vein sample, so the 1000th costs 6030 and 1000 fakes cost 3,033,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-vein ring fails: one farm cannot mint 1000 vein prints.
